text_blocks.snippet: Viral gene therapy is a technique that uses modified viruses to deliver genetic material into cells, aiming to treat or prevent diseases, particularly genetic disorders. It involves introducing therapeutic genes into a patient's cells using viral vectors, which are essentially modified viruses that have been engineered to carry and deliver the desired genetic material without causing infection.
snippet_highlighted_words: a technique that uses modified viruses to deliver genetic material into cells, aiming to treat or prevent diseases, particularly genetic disorders

list.title: Viral Vectors:
list.snippet: Viruses are naturally adept at infecting cells and delivering their genetic material. In viral gene therapy, scientists utilize this ability by modifying viruses to remove their disease-causing genes and replace them with therapeutic genes.

list.title: Delivery:
list.snippet: The modified viral vector is introduced into the patient's body, either directly into a specific tissue or systemically (e.g., intravenously). The vector then infects target cells, delivering the therapeutic gene.

list.title: Gene Expression:
list.snippet: Once inside the cell, the therapeutic gene can be expressed, leading to the production of a functional protein that can correct a genetic defect or provide some other therapeutic benefit.
